quickAnswer: For three full days in Beijing, plan the Forbidden City / Palace Museum and Jingshan, a separate Great Wall day, then Temple of Heaven with Qianmen or a hutong alternative. Arrange the order around confirmed bookings, opening days and weather; use the Monday version below if needed. Keep arrival and departure time outside the three sightseeing days, and choose one Great Wall section rather than squeezing two into the trip.

sections.title: Three days in Beijing at a glance

rows: Day 1
Tiananmen-area access check and the Forbidden City / Palace Museum
Jingshan after the museum, then a short dinner or neighbourhood walk
Day 2
One Great Wall section, with transfers planned both ways
Return to Beijing; keep the evening flexible
Day 3
Temple of Heaven on a suitable opening day
Qianmen and Dashilan; choose a hutong alternative if time and energy allow

items: Allow three full sightseeing days, plus your arrival and departure time. This is a proposed order, not a set of timed reservations.
Fix the museum date first and protect a separate Great Wall day; the Monday example below shows how to reorder the route.
Keep the Summer Palace for a fourth day or use it to replace a full city block. Avoid adding it after the Temple of Heaven and hutongs.

links.label: Beijing airport transfer: PEK or PKX
links.description: Check the airport, terminal and city transfer before counting an arrival as a sightseeing day.

sections.title: If your three days include a Monday

rows: Monday
Great Wall day
Section open, safe conditions, tickets and return transport
Tuesday
Forbidden City / Palace Museum and Jingshan
Confirmed museum date and current access arrangements
Wednesday
Temple of Heaven, then Qianmen
Charged sights open; choose the ticket for the areas you want

items: The Palace Museum normally shuts on Mondays, with statutory-holiday exceptions. Temple of Heaven’s separately charged attractions also observe Monday closures outside those exceptions; park access is a different question.

The table is a planning example for three full days, not a promise of opening or ticket availability. If the wall is closed or conditions are unsuitable, use an available city block and rebuild the sequence around confirmed bookings.

sections.title: Day 1: Beijing imperial centre
items: For each Tiananmen-area stop, check its own official access and identity instructions. A museum booking should not be treated as blanket admission to every site in the area.
Book the Palace Museum under the passport you will carry. Its published ticket window starts at 20:00 China time (UTC+8), seven days ahead; same-day ticket sales are unavailable.
Bring that original passport to Wumen / Meridian Gate (午门), the southern entrance. Plan a northbound museum visit, then consider Jingshan (景山) after exiting, subject to current access rules.

Keep the rest of the day light: a meal or short neighbourhood walk rather than another large attraction across the city. A confirmed booking and the live opening calendar take priority over this suggested sequence.

sections.title: Day 2: Great Wall day trip
items: Choose one Great Wall section. Compare Badaling and Mutianyu against your actual hotel, transport plan, walking needs and current weather.
Price and confirm the complete outbound and return journey. A train station, bus stop or scenic-area entrance is only one part of the trip.
Check which ticket covers admission, any scenic-area shuttle and any cable car; do not assume one product includes every segment.
Save the pickup or station name in Chinese, the last usable return connection and a backup before leaving. Keep the evening free for delays or fatigue.

links.label: Plan the Great Wall train or bus journey
links.description: Use the transport guide for Badaling station choices, Mutianyu bus connections and return checks.

sections.title: Day 3: Temple of Heaven, Qianmen and local Beijing
items: Use a non-Monday slot for the Temple of Heaven’s charged sights unless an official holiday exception applies. The surrounding park and the charged attractions have different access arrangements.
After the temple visit, take a metro or taxi connection to Qianmen (前门) and Dashilan (大栅栏) for food and a shorter walking block.
If hutongs are your priority, choose a Shichahai (什刹海) neighbourhood block instead of stacking it on top of every stop. Save the Chinese place name and check the transfer in your map app.
Keep the Summer Palace as a replacement or fourth-day plan. Leave the last evening near your hotel if you have an early onward departure.

items: Use the exact passport spelling consistently. A nickname, missing middle name, or wrong document number can cause avoidable booking problems.
Opening hours, ticket-release procedures, closures, and security arrangements can change. Treat this page as a route framework, not a replacement for live official notices.
Booking and closure details in this update were checked on October 22, 2026. Reconfirm official notices for your own dates; a published release window does not guarantee ticket availability.

sections.title: Where to stay for a three-day visit
items: Choose a hotel for daily transport rather than the lowest city-wide price. Being near a useful metro connection can save more time than staying near one attraction.
Wangfujing and the central east side work well for many first-time visitors who want convenient access to the imperial core, restaurants, and transport.
Qianmen can suit travellers prioritising the historic centre and Temple of Heaven, while areas farther east may suit nightlife or business-focused stays.
Confirm foreign-passport check-in, late-arrival arrangements, deposit method, breakfast time, and the hotel name and address in Chinese.

sections.title: Transport and daily pace
items: Use the metro for predictable cross-city journeys, but allow time for security, long station corridors, transfers, and choosing the correct exit.
Use licensed taxis or in-app ride-hailing for awkward connections, late returns, or travellers with mobility limits. Save the destination in Chinese and verify the licence plate.
Beijing attractions are large. A day with two nearby major sights can still involve substantial walking and standing.
Build at least one flexible block into every day. Security queues, timed entry, traffic, weather, and meal waits can shift the schedule.

sections.title: Adjust the itinerary for your trip

rows: Only two full days
Keep the imperial centre and Great Wall; remove Day 3 rather than compressing all three
Four full days
Add the Summer Palace, a deeper museum visit, or a slower neighbourhood day
Poor Great Wall weather
Swap Days 2 and 3 when reservations permit; never ignore closure or safety notices
Travelling with children
Shorten museum time, protect meal breaks, and choose a manageable Great Wall route
Limited mobility
Reduce daily stops, verify step-free access, and budget for more point-to-point transport
Monday or closure conflict
Use the Monday alternative above and check each venue’s calendar before changing a fixed booking.

items: If Beijing is part of a longer China trip, connect it with the 7-day, 10-day, or 14-day itinerary rather than planning each city independently.
For a Beijing–Shanghai route, compare an open-jaw flight plan with the live Railway 12306 schedule and the complete station locations.

faqs.question: Are three days enough for Beijing?
faqs.answer: Three full days are enough for a focused first visit: one imperial-centre day, one Great Wall day, and one Temple of Heaven plus hutong or flexible-sight day. Three hotel nights with a late arrival and early departure are not the same as three full days.

faqs.question: How should I plan three days in Beijing including a Monday?
faqs.answer: One Monday–Wednesday option is the Great Wall, then the Palace Museum, then Temple of Heaven and Qianmen. Confirm tickets, operations and weather before using that order. Holiday exceptions and current closure notices take priority.

faqs.question: Which Great Wall section is best for a first visit?
faqs.answer: Choose according to transport, walking ability, season, crowd tolerance, and live operations. Badaling has established visitor infrastructure and an official website; other sections can offer a different experience but may need more planning.

faqs.question: Do I need to book the Palace Museum in advance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the official reservation service with your passport details. Consult the booking section for the published release window and entrance, then reconfirm notices for your visit date. Do not depend on buying a ticket after arriving.

faqs.question: Can I visit the Forbidden City and Great Wall on the same day?
faqs.answer: It is not a good first-trip plan. Both need meaningful time, and combining them creates a fragile schedule with transport, security, ticket, weather, and walking risks.

faqs.question: Where should a first-time visitor stay in Beijing?
faqs.answer: A central area near a useful metro connection is usually the safest choice. Wangfujing, the central east side, and Qianmen can work, but check the exact hotel location, passport check-in, and daily routes before booking.

faqs.question: How should I get around Beijing?
faqs.answer: Combine the metro for predictable cross-city journeys with licensed taxis or app-based rides for awkward connections. Save Chinese addresses, allow for security and long station walks, and verify the car before entering.

faqs.question: Can ChinaEase Buddy personalise this Beijing itinerary?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your dates, arrival and departure points, group, interests, walking ability, hotel, budget, and fixed bookings to receive a route adapted to the actual trip.
